kernel.governing_law: The speaker commands remembrance and vigilance against an arrival that will be unknowable, excepts a remnant whose purity earns companionship, and promises the victor indelible inscription and spoken recognition before the highest witnesses.
kernel.mutated_relation: Against every promise of preservation, inscription, and recognition — the negation: the arrival that never comes to the wakeful, the garments that soil, the name unsaid before all witnesses, the book that empties.

independent.recovered_law: Every positive relation in Text A is systematically negated or inverted in Text B: remembering becomes forgetting, receiving becomes losing, the promise of coming becomes a promise of not coming, the worthy walk in white becomes the unworthy soiled in darkness, the victor clothed in white becomes stripped in filthy garments, and confessing the name becomes silencing it. The directional flow of divine grace, reward, and acknowledgment toward the faithful is reversed into absence, denial, and withholding.
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same systematic negation/inversion of every positive promise — arrival, garments, naming, inscription — into absence, soiling, silence, and emptying.
independent.terminal_note: The final portion (3:5) maintains the inversion: περιβαλεῖται ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς → γυμνωθήσεται ἐν ἱματίοις ῥυπαροῖς, ἐξαλείψω → οὐ μὴ γράψω, ὁμολογήσω → σιωπήσω — the reversed relation holds throughout.
